question: According to the national press, under the agreement signed by Pedro Sánchez and Joe Biden in May 2023, 281 Nicaraguan and Venezuelan immigrants are due to arrive in Spain. The reports also mention a pilot project providing the migrants with housing and employment. 1.
Is the Commission aware of this agreement?
Is the agreement between Spain and the US compatible with the new Pact on Migration and Asylum, adopted in trilogue on 20 December 2023?
Is the Commission aware of the above-mentioned pilot project and does it have European funding?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.4.2024) 1. The Honourable Member refers to the ‘Trilateral statement on joint commitment to Latin America’ issued by the United States, Spain and Canada on 3 May 2023. This statement is publicly available1. 2.

The legislative proposals that were put forward in the Pact on Migration and Asylum2 are the subject of on-going decision-making processes and are yet to be adopted and enter into force. The Commission cannot analyse the conformity of specific initiatives by Member States with rules that have not yet been adopted and/or are not in force. 3.

As regards the implementation of the 2021-2027 Asylum Migration and Integration Fund programme of Spain3, no payment requests have been received so far. As set out in the Fundspecific Regulation (Regulation 2021/1147)4, any project supported under this Fund should be implemented in accordance with the applicable rules.
